raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year the way I always do. I'll start with the wheat since it's already in the ground, and then figure the maize.

---

**Me talking to myself about this year's plan:**

My 9.2 mu is all in the wheat-maize rotation, same as my father did and same as I've done since I took over. I don't see any reason to change. The land knows these two crops.

For the wheat — I planted it back in October, like everyone in the village does. Used the same variety my brother-in-law uses, he gets decent yield and the seed shop down the road always has it. I saved a bit of my own seed too but mostly bought. Put down two bags of the compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15) per mu before planting — that's how my neighbor does it and my father always said two bags is right. Didn't put anything extra, money's tight and the winter rains weren't bad.

Now it's spring, wheat is waking up. I'll water it once when it's turning green, then again at jointing. If it looks yellow at jointing I'll throw down a bag of urea — maybe half a bag per mu, spread by hand when I walk the field. Last year I only topdressed half the field because I ran out of money mid-season and the part I skipped gave less. Lesson learned, this year I'll buy the urea early so I have it. If the weather stays dry I might water a third time before heading, but water costs money at the pump, so I watch the sky first.

Spray? Yes, once for weeds in spring when I see them coming up between the rows. If I see aphids later on the ears I'll spray again but usually one spray does it. My wife helps mix, I carry the sprayer.

Harvest end of June. Hire the combine — everyone uses the same guy, 60 yuan per mu. Can't do it by hand anymore on 9 mu, no time.

For the maize — soon as the wheat is off, I've got maybe 3-4 days to get maize in. No time to plow proper, I use direct seeding through the wheat stubble, hire the neighbor with the planter. Hybrid seed, has to be — you can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. Same variety as last year, Zhengdan or whatever the shop pushes, it did fine.

Put down compound fertilizer with the planter, same two bags per mu. Then at the big-trumpet stage (about knee high) I topdress urea, one bag per mu spread by hand along the rows. That's how it's always been done here.

Maize I only water if July-August is dry. Usually the rains come. If they don't, I water once, maybe twice. Costs money.

Labor — me and my wife can handle most of it. My two older kids help on weekends, youngest is still in school so I don't count on him. For harvest I hire the combine again. My brother-in-law has off-farm work in Shijiazhuang but he comes back to help for a day or two at the busy times.

Money this year — I've got maybe 6000 yuan set aside for inputs, everything. Got to make it stretch. No fancy changes, same as last year, because last year wasn't bad — wheat gave me maybe 400 kg/mu, maize maybe 450. Not great, not terrible. If I try something new and it fails, my family eats less. Not worth it.
